concept.name: Market capitalization
concept.definition: Crypto market capitalization is the total USD value of an asset's supply, conventionally computed as current price multiplied by circulating supply (Coin Metrics' on-chain variant uses all issued native units).
concept.intuition: It is the price tag of the entire network at today's price — the standard yardstick for comparing the size of cryptoassets.
concept.mechanics: Conventional market cap = circulating supply × price (reported float), while Coin Metrics' CapMrktCurUSD = current issued supply × daily close, deliberately including escrow/foundation holdings; 'free float' variants exclude insider and strategic holdings. The choice of supply basis is why different sites report different market caps for the same coin.
concept.formula: Market cap = circulating supply × price; (Coin Metrics on-chain: CapMrktCurUSD = SplyCur × PriceUSD).
concept.failure_modes: Market cap treats illiquid, lost and locked coins as if they traded at spot, overstating economically real value; for thin-float tokens, small purchases move price — and thus 'market cap' — far more than real capital committed.
concept.misconceptions: Market cap is not 'money invested' in the coin — it is a marginal price times a stock of supply, so a $1B market cap can rest on a few million dollars of actual inflows. It also says nothing about liquidity or exit capacity.
concept.example: If BTC trades at $100,000 with ~19.9M coins issued, its market cap is ~$1.99T; Coin Metrics' realized cap — each coin at its last-moved price — sits far lower, showing how much of that figure is unrealized gain.
